events.statement: The earliest ERROR log in payment-service appears at 2026-04-02T12:15:27Z, message "payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected".
The most frequent error pattern is "mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected", seen 140 times, first occurring at 2026-04-02T12:15:27Z.
A related TLS expiration error "bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); ... notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z" first appears at 2026-04-02T12:16:44Z.

events.answer: Payment failures began at 2026-04-02T12:15:27Z, triggered by mTLS handshake rejections with the bank-partner API due to an expired client certificate.

events.statement: payment-service downstream dependencies (as of latest data) include ledger-db (shared PostgreSQL), bank-partner-api (external vendor API), and kafka (shared queue).
No code deployments for payment-service were recorded in the 24‑hour window preceding the incident (2026‑04‑01T12:32Z to 2026‑04‑02T13:59Z).
A configuration change on payment-service raised the bank API timeout from 3000 ms to 5000 ms at 2026‑04‑02T11:20:00Z.

events.description: No telemetry or deployment history is available for the external bank-partner-api, so any recent changes on that side cannot be verified.

events.answer: In the past 24 hours payment‑service had no new deployments, but a config change increased its bank‑API timeout at 11:20 Z, and it depends on a shared ledger DB, a shared Kafka queue, and an external bank‑partner API.

events.statement: The outbound bank API error rate spiked from ~0.2% before 12:12 to 50.1% avg (max 100%) at 12:12 and then stayed at 100% for all subsequent buckets, matching the failure onset at 12:15:27.
The 99th‑percentile latency of calls to the bank API remained low (≈140 ms) after the error‑rate spike, showing no latency surge concurrent with the failures.

events.description: No metric named "bank_api_timeout_rate" or similar is listed among the available metrics for payment-service; cannot assess timeout rate trend.

events.answer: Downstream calls to the bank API show a sharp error‑rate increase to 100% starting at the 12:12 bucket, coinciding with the reported mTLS handshake failures, while latency stayed low; timeout‑rate data is unavailable.

events.title: Bank partner API TLS certificate expired, causing mTLS handshake rejections
Payment-service configuration change increased timeout, exposing TLS handshake failures
External bank‑partner‑api deployment introduced TLS handshake bug
Network/DNS connectivity issue between payment‑service and bank‑partner‑api

events.summary: H1 is plausible and has strong evidence for the expired TLS certificate and handshake rejections, but the causal chain relies on unverified assumptions about how payment-service translates those rejections into customer‑visible failures and why the generic HTTP error‑rate metric stays normal. We lack direct proof of the certificate expiration, of the response codes sent to customers, and of the absence of alternative causes (e.g., external API deployment or network outage).

events.why: top hypothesis is above threshold and clearly ahead
